data.current_summary: Fetch a transcript (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, or file URL)
data.current_description: Returns a transcript - text plus timestamped segments. Accepts YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram URLs (or a bare TikTok video id), direct media file URLs. Speaker ids are hints from voice separation, not named identification. When no captions exist the audio is transcribed automatically: when we can determine the media length, media under 20 minutes simply waits (the request is held open for up to 45 seconds) and returns the finished transcript, so no polling is needed; when the length cannot be determined, only short-form platforms (TikTok and Instagram) are held inline. Longer media, or a transcription still running when the 45-second hold expires, returns 202 with a job to poll instead - the work continues either way, so the same request is safe to retry and will hit the cache once it finishes. Supply callback_url to have the finished transcript POSTed to you instead of polling. Every failure carries an ai_fallback block saying whether captions were definitively unavailable and whether retrying would work.
data.summary_suggestion: Fetch video transcript with automatic audio transcription
data.description_suggestion: Fetches a transcript from a video URL (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram) or direct media file URL. Returns text transcript with timestamped segments. If captions exist, returns immediately (200). If no captions, automatically transcribes audio: videos under 20 minutes return synchronously; longer videos or those still processing after 45 seconds return 202 with a job_id for polling. Supports callback_url for asynchronous delivery. Speaker IDs indicate voice separation hints, not named speakers. Charges 1 credit for successful caption fetches; audio transcription costs 1 credit per started minute (minimum 1). Failed requests are free. Safe to retry - results are cached.

data.current_description: Returns the state of a transcription job created when a request escalated to audio. 200 for any job your account owns (an unknown id, or a job belonging to someone else, is a 404): read the status field, which is "processing" while the job is running, "completed" with the transcript in data, or "failed" with an error. The job_id and a ready-to-use poll_url come back in the 202 that started it. Free to poll on our side - credits are charged once, on delivery (1 credit per started minute of audio, minimum 1). NOTE for RapidAPI subscribers: every poll is still a billable request on your Hub plan, so prefer callback_url, or simply re-send the original request once the job has had time to finish (the result is cached, so it returns instantly and the delivery is charged once, not twice). Most transcriptions never reach this endpoint at all: when we can determine the media length, media under 20 minutes is returned synchronously, and short-form platforms (TikTok and Instagram) are held inline even when we cannot.
data.summary_suggestion: Check audio transcription job status and retrieve transcript
data.description_suggestion: Polls the status of an audio transcription job initiated by a video transcript request that escalated to async processing (202 response). Returns status field: "processing" (job running), "completed" (transcript in data field), or "failed" (with error details). Job IDs are provided in the 202 response. Polling is free on the API side; credits are charged once on delivery (1 credit per started minute of audio, minimum 1). Note: RapidAPI Hub subscribers are billed per poll request - consider using callback_url or re-sending the original request after sufficient time (results are cached and charged once). Most transcriptions complete synchronously and never require polling.

Send mode: "captions" to keep the old behaviour and have captionless entries fail as no_transcript instead.
data.description_suggestion: Fetches transcripts for up to 50-500 videos in a single request (limit depends on plan tier). Accepts YouTube, TikTok, Instagram URLs and bare YouTube IDs. Returns array of transcripts with metadata. Charges 1 credit per successful transcript; failed videos are free. Videos without captions are automatically transcribed from audio: these return with outcome "processing" and job_id, cost nothing initially, and are charged on delivery (1 credit per started minute, minimum 1). Re-send the batch after processing completes to retrieve finished transcripts - polling is optional. Set mode: "captions" to fail captionless videos instead of auto-transcribing. Batch size limits: 50 (Free/Basic/Pro), 500 (Mega/Scale). Oversized requests fail entirely before charging.
